project.subtitle: Four-Floor, Eight-Character Haunting Investigation with SRD Magic Loot
project.high_concept: Two to eight humans and enough bots to fill eight unique character seats explore a four-floor, twenty-two-room keep. One living character is privately briefed as the original killer and receives an ordinary five-card evidence hand so they can legally disprove theories without exposing their role. A different opening victim begins as a haunting ghost. Players physically enter rooms, search trapped fixtures, fight monsters, draw mundane and magical weapons and treasure, and eliminate card combinations until they can risk a final accusation.

Killer In The Keep v4.2.0 canonical_game rules

rules: All eight named characters appear in every match.
Humans choose available characters first unless random assignment is enabled.
Bots fill every remaining unique character slot.
A bot can be the original killer, the opening victim, a later victim, a secondary killer in Free For All, or a ghost.
Monster AI, trap logic, and the dungeon director are separate from character bots.
fairness: Bots receive only the information visible to their seat.
Bots cannot inspect the sealed solution, other hands, other private notes, or private chat.
Difficulty changes reasoning and tactics, not secret-data access.

modes.summary: The non-killers cooperate to survive and expose the original killer while the original killer secretly sabotages them.

evidence.shared_case_board: Only voluntarily shared or server-confirmed evidence is public.

victory.investigators: Submit the correct original killer, weapon, and room, then capture, defeat, or escape the original killer in the Final Confrontation.
victory.original_killer: Leave no eligible non-killer accuser, escape after completing the killer agenda, or let the doom clock expire with the case unsolved.
victory.ghosts: Non-killer ghosts share the investigator result; the original-killer ghost shares the killer result.

modes.summary: All characters investigate independently. PvP, betrayal, theft, private accusations, and multiple later killers are possible.

pvp.secondary_killer_trigger: A non-original-killer who intentionally causes another playable character's permanent death becomes a hidden Secondary Killer.
pvp.sealed_case_never_changes: Secondary killers never replace the original killer, weapon, or room.

evidence.sharing: Voluntary, tradable, stealable only through explicit rules, and bluffable in speech.
evidence.server_truth: Card identities, inventory, dice, and system logs cannot be falsified.

victory.case_victor: The first living character to make a correct accusation and survive the Final Confrontation wins the case.
victory.original_killer: Wins by completing the killer agenda and escaping or by leaving no eligible living accuser.
victory.secondary_killer: Can win a configured elimination objective, such as becoming the last living independent character, but cannot win by claiming the original case.
victory.ranking: Case victory has priority; survival, killer agenda, eliminations, treasure, confirmed deductions, and time determine placement.

original_killer.evidence_participation: The killer has a normal private evidence hand, must reveal every matching card during disproof exactly like any other living seat, and cannot refuse a server-enforced reveal.
original_killer.cover_theories: The killer may submit legal non-final room theories for cover, but cannot win by submitting the solution they were told.

opening_victim.body_location: A legal unoccupied cell in the sealed murder room.
opening_victim.human_playable_victim: The player watches the off-screen opening death, starts as a ghost, cannot report their own body, and has all starting cards returned to their source decks before active play.
opening_victim.bot_playable_victim: The bot starts as a ghost bot under the same limits.
opening_victim.ghost_spawn: same legal map cell as their body inside the murder room
opening_victim.does_not_learn_killer_identity: The opening murder occurs off-screen. The victim knows they were killed but not who killed them unless a later legal clue reveals it.
opening_victim.ghost_start: The victim starts at the body in Ghost Mode and can haunt immediately under normal Haunt Energy rules.
opening_victim.information_limit: The victim does not automatically learn the killer unless an authored cinematic visibly identifies the killer.

setup_sequence: Select one original-killer Character card, one evidence Weapon card, and one Room card for the server-only envelope.
Select a different active character as the opening victim.
Privately brief the killer with role, victim, murder room, murder weapon, cover objectives, and killer victory condition.
Place the victim body in the murder room and transition that seat directly to Ghost Mode.
Shuffle the remaining 35 evidence cards and deal exactly 5 cards to each of the 7 living players/bots, including the killer.
Privately show each living seat its five-card hand. No UI or network payload identifies which hand belongs to the killer.
Place living tokens at the mode-specific starter cells, subject only to a safe opening-body conflict adjustment.
Instantiate authored locks, fixed traps, hidden monsters, containers, searchable fixtures, and configured random traps.

sabotage lights, wards, doors, objectives, and selected keep systems

create noise or bait that influences Monster-deck aggro
use discovered passages under normal discovery rules unless a character power says otherwise
lie, frame, report, discuss, vote, and accuse
original_killer.combat_rule: The opening murder may be cinematic. Every later attempted murder uses the ordinary D&D-style combat, damage, downed, rescue, and death systems.
original_killer.if_killed: Becomes an original-killer ghost and continues hostile haunting, but cannot make living-character attacks or living accusations.

secondary_killers.creation: Intentional permanent playable-character kill by a non-original-killer.
secondary_killers.knowledge: A secondary killer is privately told their new status and objective.
secondary_killers.case_integrity: Later murders are recorded separately; the opening solution envelope never changes.
possible_objectives: be the last living independent character
frame the original killer or another secondary killer
survive until the original case resolves

count_clarification.one_armory_weapon_deck: Mundane and selected magic physical weapon cards found at racks, caches, and weapon rewards.
count_clarification.separation_rule: Evidence Weapon cards never become equippable weapon objects. Armory Weapon cards never enter the sealed murder envelope.

treasure_deck.screen_behavior: The card appears and can be kept, equipped, traded, consumed, or returned according to its rules.
treasure_deck.permanent_death: All held deck-owned Treasure cards return to the Treasure deck and shuffle.
treasure_deck.mundane_weapon_separation: Ordinary nonmagical weapons are drawn from the Armory Weapon deck, not the Treasure deck.
treasure_deck.magic_weapon_separation: Magic weapons are Weapon-deck cards, not Treasure-deck cards, unless an authored quest explicitly awards a named weapon card.

monster_deck.contents: Keep-appropriate monster encounter cards with current/max HP data.
monster_deck.screen_behavior: Reveal the monster card, spawn it on the nearest legal square, show an HP bar, and enter initiative when hostile.
monster_deck.resolution: Affected living characters enter initiative. The monster can be defeated, escaped, contained, befriended if allowed, or left persistent in the room.
monster_deck.ghost_interaction: Ghosts may influence legal movement, patrol destination, room interest, or aggression cues but cannot make illegal attacks.
monster_deck.permanent_death: Held summon or control cards return to the Monster deck. Independent active monsters remain until their encounter resolves.
monster_deck.automatic_authored_spawns: All nine mapped monster instances exist at match setup, hidden at their authored cells.

trap_deck.purpose: Represent fixed trap cards referenced by the map and random temporary traps.
draw_triggers: interact with an authored trapped door, passage, chest, or bookshelf
trap_deck.screen_behavior: The card pops up, places a legal temporary hazard, displays counters, and starts a synchronized countdown.
trap_deck.disarm: Use a D&D-style Search and tool sequence: detect with Passive Perception or a Search action using Wisdom (Perception), study mechanisms with Intelligence (Investigation) when useful, and disarm a mechanical trap with a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the trap disable DC. Tool proficiency adds Proficiency Bonus; matching skill proficiency grants Advantage under the revised tool rule. Magical traps may instead allow Intelligence (Arcana), Dispel Magic, a listed spell, or a card-specific counter.
trap_deck.success: Disable the trap, gain XP, and receive configured Treasure or Gameplay rewards.
trap_deck.failure: Apply damage, conditions, alarm, separation, lockdown, monster draw, or environmental effects.
trap_deck.ghost_interaction: Every ghost can trigger an armed trap or spend Haunt Energy to draw and place a new legal Trap card.
trap_deck.fairness: No random trap may spawn on a protected starting cell, meeting zone, inaccessible tile, or unavoidable no-counterplay route.
trap_deck.permanent_death: Unused held Trap cards return to the Trap deck. Resolved cards enter discard and reshuffle when needed.

monster_trigger_cards.rule: Some Trap cards do not deal their main effect directly. They instruct the active seat to draw a Monster card, spawn that monster on a valid adjacent or room spawn cell, show its HP bar, and begin initiative.

trap_deck.monster_ambush: Instead of placing a normal hazard, draw the top Monster card and spawn that monster on the nearest legal unoccupied cell.
trap_deck.detection_and_disarm: Use the D&D interaction procedure defined in dnd_video_game_engine.search_locks_and_traps.

applies_to: failed death saves or other permanent death

global_card_return_on_permanent_death.solution_protection: Envelope cards never move, redraw, replace, or return.
global_card_return_on_permanent_death.opening_victim_exception: The opening victim dies before evidence is dealt and therefore returns no starting hand.

weapon_deck.contents: Thirty-six keep-appropriate revised-rules weapons: all non-firearm Simple and Martial weapons from the referenced 2024 Basic Rules table.
draw_triggers: open a weapon-bearing chest or hidden weapon cache

Use the Search or Investigate interaction.
Resolve any authored monster trigger or hidden trap attached to the rack.
Draw exactly one Weapon card from the authoritative Weapon deck.
Reveal the physical weapon to the drawing seat and add it to inventory.
Mark that rack spent unless a rule explicitly refreshes it.

proficiency_and_use.rule: Anyone may attempt to wield a weapon, but only a proficient character adds Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls.
proficiency_and_use.game_classification: A weapon is class-compatible when the character is proficient through class or an explicit character override.
proficiency_and_use.unusable_item_definition: A found Weapon-deck item for which the character lacks proficiency or cannot satisfy a required property such as Heavy ability minimum.
proficiency_and_use.mastery: Mastery activates only when the character has a feature that unlocks that mastery for the weapon.

unusable_weapon_hoarding_penalty.applies_to: Weapon-deck cards carried but not class-compatible/effectively usable by the carrier.

trade it to another living character

trade_requirements: same room or adjacent legal squares
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.transfer: The physical Weapon card moves from donor inventory to recipient inventory.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.receiver_bonus: When the recipient is proficient with the traded weapon, the recipient upgrades their own currently equipped signature weapon to +1.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.plus_one_effect: +1 to attack rolls and +1 to damage rolls made with the upgraded weapon.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.recipient_choice: The recipient may instead designate the newly received weapon as their own equipped weapon and apply the +1 to it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.non_stacking: A character’s trade upgrade stops at +1. Further trades do not produce +2 or higher unless a separate explicit rule grants it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.anti_loop: Each physical Weapon card can trigger this trade upgrade once per match, and trading the same card back and forth never retriggers it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.movement_update: The donor’s hoarding penalty recalculates immediately after the weapon leaves their inventory.

weapon_deck.death_return: All held Weapon-deck cards return face down to the Weapon deck and the deck is shuffled before control transfers fully to Ghost Mode.

evidence_deck.solution_setup: Seal one Character, one evidence Weapon, and one Room card server-side.
evidence_deck.starting_deal: After sealing three solution cards and selecting the separate opening victim, deal all 35 remaining evidence cards as seven private five-card hands. Every living seat—including the killer—receives one hand. The opening-victim ghost receives none.
evidence_deck.private_hands: Only the owning authenticated seat and server-authoritative bot logic can see a hand.
evidence_deck.physical_room_disproof: During a legal room theory, every living player/bot holding any named card plays every matching card face-up into the temporary Disproof Zone. Cards return to their owners after all living players see them.
evidence_deck.keep_deck_after_death: Evidence cards held by a later permanently dead character return face down to the protected Keep deck. During a legal theory, the server also plays every matching Keep-deck card to the Disproof Zone, then reshuffles it.
evidence_deck.opening_victim_hand: The opening victim receives no cards because the victim is dead before the 35-card deal.
evidence_deck.card_face_restriction: Evidence cards identify only their character, evidence weapon, or room and may not mention traps, locks, secret passages, searchable fixtures, hidden items, monster spawns, or treasure.
evidence_deck.killer_hand_rule: The killer hand is indistinguishable in size, card backs, network schema, and UI from every other living hand. The killer must publicly play all matching cards during disproof.
evidence_deck.room_theory: Any living, conscious character, including the killer for cover, may make a legal room theory from the room they physically occupy. The theorist may not name cards in their own hand.
evidence_deck.final_accusation_killer_restriction: The original killer cannot submit or win through a Final Accusation because they were given the solution at setup.

armory_weapon_deck.source_basis: Mundane weapon statistics use SRD 5.2.1. Magic inserts use SRD 5.2.1 magic items and retain their named extra energy/damage types.
armory_weapon_deck.official_rule_note: Official D&D permits anyone to wield a weapon but withholds the Proficiency Bonus when the wielder lacks proficiency.
armory_weapon_deck.killer_in_the_keep_override: For this game, a character who is not compatible with a found weapon cannot equip or attack with it; they may carry or trade it.
armory_weapon_deck.draw_rule: Investigate a weapon rack and resolve its Search/encounter trigger, then draw and reveal exactly one top card from this deck. Determine compatibility only after the card is revealed.

carry_penalty.applies_to: Each carried Armory Weapon card the carrier cannot use.
carry_penalty.legacy_roll_movement: Subtract 1 traversable grid square from the movement die result per incompatible carried weapon; minimum final result 0 squares.
carry_penalty.tactical_speed_equivalent: Subtract 5 feet of movement per incompatible carried weapon for the turn; minimum 0 feet after all modifiers.
carry_penalty.equipped_or_compatible_cards: No penalty from compatible weapons, equipped weapons, evidence Weapon cards, or non-weapon treasure.

requirements: Both characters are living and conscious.
Both occupy the same named room or adjacent legal grid cells.
Recipient is compatible with the traded weapon.
Trade is accepted by the recipient or their bot logic.
trade_rule.enhancement: The recipient immediately gives their currently equipped weapon a permanent +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls for the remainder of the match.
trade_rule.stacking: Bonuses can stack to a maximum of +3 on one equipped weapon.
trade_rule.anti_exploit: Each Armory Weapon card can grant this enhancement only once. After granting it, mark the card bound_to_upgrade and remove it from further trade loops until match end.
trade_rule.unequipped_recipient: If the recipient has no equipped weapon, they equip the received weapon and it becomes +1.

haunting_actions.effect: Set off an already armed built-in or Trap-deck trap when a legal trigger exists.
Draw the top Trap card and place it on a server-approved tile in the current or adjacent connected room.

mode_behavior.work_together: Non-killer ghosts remain aligned with the investigators; the original-killer ghost remains hostile.
mode_behavior.free_for_all: Ghosts retain personal loyalties and may help, hinder, bargain through séances, or pursue haunting objectives.

progression.game_level: A ghost keeps the Game Level reached at death.
progression.ghost_upgrades: Living upgrades are replaced by level-scaled haunting upgrades until revival.
progression.revival: A revived character returns to living movement and abilities. Cards already returned to decks remain in circulation.

security: Ghost clients never receive the server-only solution.
Ghost vision cannot automatically update a living shared notebook.
Ghosts cannot place unavoidable traps or force illegal monster attacks.

body_report.effect: Open the meeting interface while preserving persistent monsters, traps, bodies, and cards.

discussion.seance: An explicit séance can open a short, limited ghost-to-living channel without permitting a vote or direct card reveal.

vote.default_result: A unique highest non-skip target is banished.

banishment_profiles.lethal: The target permanently dies, returns cards, and becomes a ghost.
banishment_profiles.nonlethal: The target is imprisoned or disabled for a configured duration.

vote.does_not_solve_case: Voting never replaces the original killer + weapon + room final accusation.

room_theory_algorithm: Verify the accuser is a living non-killer and physically occupies a solution-eligible room.
Set the accused room to the accuser’s current room; the UI cannot name a different room.
Accept one suspected original-killer Character card and one murder-evidence Weapon card.
Block any Character, Weapon, or Room card currently in the accuser’s own evidence hand; an accusation is based on cards the accuser does not have.
Ask every living evidence holder, including bots, to play all named cards they hold. Each played card turns face-up publicly and proves that category choice is not in the envelope.
The original killer has no evidence hand and therefore cannot play a disproof card.
If no living hand plays a card, check the shuffled Gameplay Keep deck containing evidence returned by dead characters.
Reveal every matching Keep-deck card and mark it public; the accusation is disproved if any match exists.
If no living hand and no Keep-deck card can disprove the exact three-card combination, offer the eligible accuser the choice to continue investigating or lock it in as the Final Accusation.
Record all played cards on the public case board and every legal private inference in the accuser’s notebook.

final_accusation.room_validation: The submitted room must equal the room currently occupied by the accuser. Either Library floor counts as the Library.
eligibility: has not used strict final accusation
holds none of the three submitted cards
exact combination was not disproved in the immediately preceding Room Accusation
final_accusation.work_together: The team confirms a shared Final Accusation from the physical room. A wrong strict accusation grants the original killer victory unless forgiving mode is enabled.
final_accusation.free_for_all: Each eligible living non-killer gets one strict Final Accusation. A wrong accuser follows the configured lethal consequence, returns all cards, and becomes a ghost without learning which field was wrong.
final_accusation.correct: Reveal the opening murder reconstruction, the original killer, weapon, victim, and room, then begin the configured Final Confrontation/capture/escape sequence.
final_accusation.killer_restriction: The original killer knows the solution but can never submit it as a winning accusation.
requirements: holds none of the three accused cards
no active meeting or unresolved forced encounter
final_accusation.resolution: Lock the request atomically, compare all three categories to the sealed envelope, then begin the Final Confrontation on a correct result.
final_accusation.wrong_work_together: Apply the configured strict-team failure or remove that accuser’s future accusation eligibility.
final_accusation.wrong_free_for_all: The accuser permanently dies, returns all deck-owned cards, and immediately becomes a ghost.
final_accusation.precheck: Before opening the envelope, repeat the public living-hand and Keep-deck disproof check. If any named card is found, reveal it, record the disproof, and cancel escalation without exposing the envelope.

privacy: The sealed solution stays server-only until a correct Final Accusation or post-match reveal.
Starting evidence hands are private to living non-killer seats.
Legally played disproof cards become public face-up evidence.
Ghosts have no evidence hand and cannot accuse, report, vote, or communicate unrestricted solution information.
The opening victim does not learn the killer merely by entering Ghost Mode.

location_requirement.room_theory: A living, conscious character must physically occupy a legal cell in the named room.
location_requirement.final_accusation: A living, conscious character must physically occupy a legal cell in the accused room.
location_requirement.library: Either Library floor area satisfies the Library location requirement.
location_requirement.not_rooms: Hallways, stairs, service passages, landings, and secret-passage transit cells cannot host a theory or accusation.

not_holding_requirement.rule: The accuser may name only a Character, evidence Weapon, and occupied Room card that are absent from the accuser’s own hand.
not_holding_requirement.client_validation: Disable any card the player holds and reject tampered requests server-side.
not_holding_requirement.reasoning: A player’s own cards already prove those elements are not in the envelope.

room_theory_sequence: A living, conscious character physically enters a solution room and chooses Room Theory.
The current room is filled automatically. The theorist names one Character and one evidence Weapon that are absent from their own hand.
The server validates occupancy, hand restrictions, living status, and unresolved encounter state.
In deterministic seat order, every living human or bot—including the original killer—who holds one or more named cards must play every matching card face-up into the public Disproof Zone.
The server also checks the protected Keep deck for matching cards returned by later dead characters and plays every match.
After the reveal window, played cards return to the correct private hand or protected Keep deck; the public case board records each disproved element.
If no card is played, mark an Unrefuted Lead and offer the theorist the option to escalate to a Final Accusation if otherwise eligible.
deduction_and_accusation.bot_behavior: Bots, including a killer bot, maintain private five-card evidence hands, refuse theories containing their own cards, and automatically play every required matching card.
deduction_and_accusation.ghost_rule: Ghosts cannot make theories, play living evidence cards, or accuse.

killer_evidence_rule.server_enforcement: A matching killer card is auto-committed to the Disproof Zone under the same timing and animation as every other matching card.
killer_evidence_rule.privacy: The reveal identifies the card owner seat, not that seat’s secret role.
killer_evidence_rule.final_accusation: The original killer cannot make a Final Accusation.

terminology.game_level: The only level number shown for in-session progression. Valid values are 1 through 5.
terminology.dnd_equivalent_level: The D&D power snapshot represented by that Game Level. It is not an additional progression track.
terminology.keep_rank: Deprecated term. Do not display or use it for canonical gameplay.

five_game_levels.clarification: Five Game Levels means five total level states in a session. Players start at Game Level 1 and can level up four times, ending at Game Level 5. It does not mean five additional level-ups after the starting level.

level_table.ability_jump: Begin with the complete curated D&D level 5-equivalent hero package, including the hero's unlimited powers, starting limited powers, starting equipment, and level-appropriate combat statistics.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 9-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 2. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 13-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 3. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.

Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 17-equivalent package. This is a major high-tier class-feature, armor, resource, spell, save DC, and combat-stat jump even when no new named power is listed.

level_table.session_role: Fourth and final level-up / session maximum
level_table.ability_jump: Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 20-equivalent package, unlock the final named powers, and apply the hero's session capstone. No progression beyond Game Level 5 is permitted during the session.

ability_jump_policy.snapshot_rule: Each Game Level is a curated destination package. On level-up, the character sheet immediately applies the destination D&D-equivalent statistics, class features, spell access, resource limits, armor improvements, and assigned powers.
ability_jump_policy.no_intermediate_processing: Do not make the player process each skipped D&D level one at a time. Only choices explicitly included in the destination package receive prompts.
ability_jump_policy.power_unlock_rule: Named powers are assigned by Game Level. Existing powers may also receive damage, range, duration, target-count, save DC, resource, or use-count upgrades at every Game Level.
ability_jump_policy.maximum_rule: When Game Level 5 is reached, further XP or level-up triggers cannot increase the character level during that session.

on_level_up: Advance exactly one Game Level, never more than one level from a single resolved trigger.
Apply the destination D&D-equivalent character package immediately.
Restore the hero to full health in Legacy mode.
Increase maximum health by 5 in Legacy mode.
Increase limited-power uses to equal the new Game Level unless a specific power states otherwise.
Unlock the named powers and class-specific upgrades assigned to the new Game Level.
Apply any armor, spell, proficiency, save DC, resource, or capstone upgrades assigned to the destination package.
Stop all further in-session leveling after Game Level 5.

valid_triggers: Roll a natural 20 during combat when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach the cumulative XP threshold for the next Game Level.
Correctly identify two previously unknown solution cards when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach a configured story milestone or objective checkpoint.
trigger_resolution.same_event_limit: A single event can grant at most one Game Level even if it satisfies multiple triggers.
trigger_resolution.maximum_level_guard: Ignore or convert additional level-up triggers into non-level rewards after Game Level 5.

health_bars.players_and_character_bots: Every living player character and character bot has a current/max HP bar in the party/roster HUD and above the token when targeted or damaged.

search_locks_and_traps.search_action: Use an action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check against the fixture’s notice/detection DC to find a concealed trap, lock detail, hidden chest, secret latch, or concealed object.
search_locks_and_traps.passive_perception: Passive Perception can provide a warning that something is wrong, but this game still requires the active Perception roll before safely manipulating a chest, bookshelf, trapped door, or secret passage.
search_locks_and_traps.authored_trap_card: If a fixture has trap_ref/card_ref, reveal that exact Trap card after detection or triggering. Otherwise draw the top random Trap card when the fixture is marked trapped.
search_locks_and_traps.disarm_action: Use a Utilize action and make a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the authored disable DC; default DC 15 when no DC is supplied.
search_locks_and_traps.lockpick_action: Picking a lock is separate from disarming its trap: make a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the authored lock DC; default DC 15 when none is supplied.
order_for_locked_and_trapped_fixture: Pick, force, magically open, or bypass lock
search_locks_and_traps.help: A nearby proficient ally can take the Help action to grant Advantage on the next applicable skill or tool check.
search_locks_and_traps.crowbar: A crowbar grants Advantage on Strength checks where leverage applies.
search_locks_and_traps.brute_force_house_rule: Without Thieves’ Tools, a character may attempt Strength (Athletics) against lock DC + 3. The attempt is noisy, cannot delicately disarm the trap, may damage contents, and may activate a monster trigger.
search_locks_and_traps.failure: A failed disarm normally triggers the trap. A failed lockpick jams or alarms the fixture only when its card or authored data says so.

fixture_investigation.chests: Every chest uses Search → trap resolution → lock resolution → Treasure draw/reveal. Authored contents are revealed as their listed Treasure cards; an unspecified chest draws the top Treasure card.

bookshelves.sequence: Search for traps or hidden mechanisms. On a trapped result, resolve a Trap card; on a monster-ambush result, draw and spawn from the Monster deck. After safe resolution, draw from the Treasure deck or reveal the authored room reward.
bookshelves.library_spider: The attached Library bookshelf search can activate the authored hidden spider at L13.

fixture_investigation.weapon_racks: Search/investigate the rack, resolve its monster or trap trigger, then draw one Armory Weapon card.

health_bars.players_and_bots: Always show current HP and maximum HP to the owning player; show teammates/opponents according to mode visibility settings.
health_bars.bloodied_marker: Display Bloodied at half maximum HP or fewer.
health_bars.monsters: All monster entities store current/max HP and display an HP bar once discovered.

free_for_all_death_saves.damage_at_zero: One failure; a critical hit causes two; damage at least equal to maximum HP causes death.
free_for_all_death_saves.stabilize: A living helper can use an action and succeed on DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine); a Healer’s Kit can stabilize according to its item rules.

hp_death_and_ghost_transition.revival: If a legal revival restores life, evidence and Treasure cards already returned remain in circulation; do not recreate duplicates.

door_and_passage_rules.protected_lock_rule: Every entrance into either guest quarter or either alchemist room begins locked, including hidden or secret entries.
lock_resolution: Use the correct key if found.
Pick the lock with a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using Thieves’ Tools against the map lock DC; default DC 15 when unspecified.
Break or pry the entry with a listed Strength (Athletics) or tool action if the object permits it; this is noisy and can trigger monsters.
Use a spell or class feature that explicitly opens, bypasses, transforms, or destroys the barrier.
door_and_passage_rules.trap_detection: Before touching a suspicious door or passage, use Passive Perception or the Search action with Wisdom (Perception) against its notice/discovery DC. Intelligence (Investigation) may identify how it works after detection.
door_and_passage_rules.trap_disarm: Mechanical traps normally use Dexterity with Thieves’ Tools against the trap disable DC. Magical traps use the card’s listed Arcana, spell, or feature counter.
door_and_passage_rules.secret_passages: Secret passages remain server-hidden until discovered. Discovery never appears on a Room card. Passage use normally ends movement for that turn.
failed_entry_consequences: tool damage where the card says so
door_and_passage_rules.locked_door_legacy: Roll 1d10 with a lockpick; 7 or higher succeeds and a natural 1 loses the lockpick.
door_and_passage_rules.trapped_door_legacy: DC 16 Dexterity saving throw to disarm; failure triggers a trap.
door_and_passage_rules.large_statue_legacy: DC 17 Strength check to move a statue blocking a secret passage.
door_and_passage_rules.dnd_conversion: Use Perception or Investigation to find, thieves' tools to disarm or unlock, and Athletics to force or move obstacles.

in_match_progression.clarification: Five Game Levels means five total level states in a session. Players start at Game Level 1 and can level up four times, ending at Game Level 5. It does not mean five additional level-ups after the starting level.

level_table.ability_jump: Begin with the complete curated D&D level 5-equivalent hero package, including the hero's unlimited powers, starting limited powers, starting equipment, and level-appropriate combat statistics.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 9-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 2. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 13-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 3. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.

Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 17-equivalent package. This is a major high-tier class-feature, armor, resource, spell, save DC, and combat-stat jump even when no new named power is listed.

level_table.ability_jump: Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 20-equivalent package, unlock the final named powers, and apply the hero's session capstone. No progression beyond Game Level 5 is permitted during the session.

ability_jump_policy.snapshot_rule: Each Game Level is a curated destination package. On level-up, the character sheet immediately applies the destination D&D-equivalent statistics, class features, spell access, resource limits, armor improvements, and assigned powers.
ability_jump_policy.no_intermediate_processing: Do not make the player process each skipped D&D level one at a time. Only choices explicitly included in the destination package receive prompts.
ability_jump_policy.power_unlock_rule: Named powers are assigned by Game Level. Existing powers may also receive damage, range, duration, target-count, save DC, resource, or use-count upgrades at every Game Level.
ability_jump_policy.maximum_rule: When Game Level 5 is reached, further XP or level-up triggers cannot increase the character level during that session.

on_level_up: Advance exactly one Game Level, never more than one level from a single resolved trigger.
Apply the destination D&D-equivalent character package immediately.
Restore the hero to full health in Legacy mode.
Increase maximum health by 5 in Legacy mode.
Increase limited-power uses to equal the new Game Level unless a specific power states otherwise.
Unlock the named powers and class-specific upgrades assigned to the new Game Level.
Apply any armor, spell, proficiency, save DC, resource, or capstone upgrades assigned to the destination package.
Stop all further in-session leveling after Game Level 5.

valid_triggers: Roll a natural 20 during combat when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach the cumulative XP threshold for the next Game Level.
Correctly identify two previously unknown solution cards when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach a configured story milestone or objective checkpoint.
trigger_resolution.same_event_limit: A single event can grant at most one Game Level even if it satisfies multiple triggers.
trigger_resolution.maximum_level_guard: Ignore or convert additional level-up triggers into non-level rewards after Game Level 5.

dnd_research_notes.rules_baseline: 2024 revised fifth-edition rules as represented by D&D Beyond Basic Rules and SRD 5.2.1.
weapon_findings: Weapons are categorized as Simple or Martial and as Melee or Ranged.
A character without weapon proficiency may wield a weapon but does not add Proficiency Bonus to the attack roll.
Properties include Ammunition, Finesse, Heavy, Light, Loading, Range, Reach, Thrown, Two-Handed, and Versatile.
Mastery properties are gated behind a feature that grants mastery use.
The default keep Weapon deck omits firearms to preserve the medieval-fantasy setting.
trap_and_lock_findings: Passive Perception can notice hidden danger without an active roll.
The Search action commonly uses Wisdom (Perception) to detect a trap.
Thieves’ Tools use Dexterity and list DC 15 for picking a lock or disarming a trap in the revised equipment rules.
Tool proficiency adds Proficiency Bonus; matching skill proficiency grants Advantage on the tool check.
